note: Benchmark manifest for `python -m nctool compare` (core/conversion-versioning): the FIXED set of scans + recipes two builds are compared over. Cases name frames; the asset inventory (paths + sha256) stays in <asset-root>/manifest.json, which `compare run` resolves them through -- there is deliberately only one asset inventory. Recipe paths are repo-relative and reuse the frozen real-scan recipes so a comparison runs the same parameters the verification harness does.

fixtures.note: The committed decoder fixtures -- tiny (502x462), no Drive assets needed, so `compare` is runnable and testable on any checkout. Covers both input formats (HDR 48-bit, HDRi 64-bit) and, across cases, a 16-bit TIFF and f32 output. This is the set to use for a determinism / zero-diff check. Each case's `args` go to every build; `destination_args` go only to a build that takes destinations (pipeline_version >= 8) and `preset_args` only to one that takes presets (the reference build, scripts/reference-snapshot/), chosen by `compare run` from the binary's --version banner. The two name the same TIFF output: the default destination (SDR Display P3 16-bit TIFF, no flag) against the `display-p3` preset, and `--film-master` against the `film-master` preset -- the same container, so a diff across the two differs in the pipeline, not the units. This is a holding set -- nf-verification/benchmark-set rebuilds it.

rolls.note: The real-scan benchmark: exposed frames from the Ektar and Phoenix rolls (the two rolls docs/reports/v0-baseline.md was measured on), each with its roll's frozen recipe from scripts/real-scan-verify/recipes/ -- so the roll-fixed Dmin comes from that roll's own calibration rather than a per-frame estimate. Requires the nc-assets Drive folder via ../nc-assets plus a generated manifest.json. The frozen recipes are recipe_version 2 documents, so this set runs only on a build that takes destinations (pipeline_version >= 8); benchmark an older build with the nctool and recipes of its own checkout.
